# Tweet Scraper V2 - X Scraper / Twitter Scraper / X.com Scraper

The Apify actor [`apidojo/tweet-scraper`](https://apify.com/apidojo/tweet-scraper) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its build **0.0.1558**. The module's version is that build number, and every run it starts is pinned to exactly that build, so the input types below are the ones the actor really runs with.

Lightning-fast search, URL, list, and profile scraping, with customizable filters. At $0.40 per 1000 tweets, and 30-80 tweets per second, it is ideal for researchers, entrepreneurs, and businesses! Get comprehensive insights from Twitter (X) now!

## Pricing

Pay per event — tweet $0.0004 (Free-plan prices; paid plans pay less). Cap the spend with `maxTotalChargeUsd`.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/apidojo/tweet-scraper) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/apidojo-tweet-scraper@0.0.1558#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs: {}
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `startUrls` | array |  |  | Start URLs — Twitter (X) URLs. Paste the URLs and get the results immediately. Tweet, Profile, Search or List URLs are supported. |
| `searchTerms` | array |  |  | Search Terms — Search terms you want to search from Twitter (X). You can refer to https://github.com/igorbrigadir/twitter-advanced-search. |
| `twitterHandles` | array |  |  | Twitter handles — Twitter handles that you want to search on Twitter (X) |
| `conversationIds` | array |  |  | Conversation IDs — Conversation IDs that you want to search on Twitter (X) |
| `maxItems` | integer |  |  | Maximum number of items on output — Maximum number of items that you want as output. |
| `sort` | string |  |  | Sort By — Sorts search results. If you are getting low results, try Top instead of Latest. Latest + Top runs both simultaneously to maximize results but may return some duplicate tweets. |
| `tweetLanguage` | string |  |  | Tweet language — Restricts tweets to the given language, given by an ISO 639-1 code. |
| `onlyVerifiedUsers` | boolean |  |  | Only verified users — If selected, only returns tweets by users who are verified. |
| `onlyTwitterBlue` | boolean |  |  | Only Twitter Blue — If selected, only returns tweets by users who are Twitter Blue subscribers. |
| `onlyImage` | boolean |  |  | Only image — If selected, only returns tweets that contain images. |
| `onlyVideo` | boolean |  |  | Only video — If selected, only returns tweets that contain videos. |
| `onlyQuote` | boolean |  |  | Only quote — If selected, only returns tweets that are quotes. |
| `author` | string |  |  | Tweet author — Returns tweets sent by the given user. It should be a Twitter (X) Handle. |
| `inReplyTo` | string |  |  | In reply to — Returns tweets that are replies to the given user. It should be a Twitter (X) Handle. |
| `mentioning` | string |  |  | Mentioning — Returns tweets mentioning the given user. It should be a Twitter (X) Handle. |
| `geotaggedNear` | string |  |  | Geotagged near — Returns tweets sent near the given location. |
| `withinRadius` | string |  |  | Within radius — Returns tweets sent within the given radius of the given location. |
| `geocode` | string |  |  | Geocode — Returns tweets sent by users located within a given radius of the given latitude/longitude. |
| `placeObjectId` | string |  |  | Place object ID — Returns tweets tagged with the given place. |
| `minimumRetweets` | integer |  |  | Minimum retweets — Returns tweets with at least the given number of retweets. |
| `minimumFavorites` | integer |  |  | Minimum favorites — Returns tweets with at least the given number of favorites. |
| `minimumReplies` | integer |  |  | Minimum replies — Returns tweets with at least the given number of replies. |
| `start` | string |  |  | Start date — Returns tweets sent after the given date. |
| `end` | string |  |  | End date — Returns tweets sent before the given date. |
| `includeSearchTerms` | boolean |  |  | Include Search Terms — If selected, a field will be added to each tweets about the search term that was used to find it. |
| `customMapFunction` | string \| null |  |  | Custom map function — Function that takes each of the objects as argument and returns data that will be mapped by the function itself. This function is not intended for filtering, please don't use it for filtering purposes or you will get banned automatically. |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
